name: EU GMP Annex 22 and Annex 11
blurb: The first GMP rules written for AI in medicine manufacturing.
title: EU GMP Annex 22 and Annex 11
answer: Draft Annex 22 sets out how AI models may be used in the manufacture of medicines and active substances: intended use defined, test data independent of training data, performance criteria set in advance, and human review where needed. It was released with a revised Annex 11 on computerised systems and Chapter 4 on documentation, together forming one framework for digital manufacturing.

reading.body:
Draft Annex 22 is the first GMP rule written specifically for AI in medicine manufacturing, and it treats a model as a system to be locked and validated, not one that keeps learning in production.

The requirements are procedural rather than technical. Intended use must be defined, test data must be independent of training data, performance criteria must be set in advance, and human review is required where needed. The draft favours static, deterministic models for critical uses. That combination points to a specific posture: freeze the model, then validate it the way any other computerised system is validated.

It matters for AI because it constrains where the compute goes. A model that cannot be retrained in place, and whose test data must be held separate from its training data, needs a fixed artefact and a documented pipeline around it. Annex 22 was released alongside a revised Annex 11 on computerised systems and Chapter 4 on documentation, so the three form one framework for digital manufacturing rather than three separate obligations.

The data covers the shape of the draft and the fact of the joint European Commission and PIC/S consultation opened on 7 July 2025. It does not give the consultation's outcome, a final adoption date, or any detail on how compliance would be evidenced in practice.

terms.line: The field of computer science dedicated to creating systems that perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence: understanding language, recognizing patterns, making decisions.

Models that create new content, text, images, video, audio, code, from patterns learned in training data. The 2022 shift from AI that classifies to AI that produces is what put this glossary on your reading list.

The subset of AI focused on systems that learn from data and improve with experience rather than following explicitly programmed rules. Nearly everything called AI in production is machine learning underneath.
The 2026 package of targeted amendments to the EU AI Act, deferring high-risk deadlines and restructuring conformity assessment.

The requirement that a person can understand, intervene in, and override AI decisions. Mandated for high-risk uses under the EU AI Act, and only real when the human has the time, information, and authority to actually intervene.

explainer:
Annex 22 is the first set of GMP rules written specifically for artificial intelligence. It applies to AI models used in the manufacture of medicines and active substances where they affect product quality, patient safety or data integrity, and it builds on Annex 11, which covers computerised systems generally.

The draft asks manufacturers to define each model's intended use precisely, involve process experts in that definition, and set performance acceptance criteria before testing. Test data must be independent of training data and representative of real conditions, and test results must show the model meets its criteria. In operation, models need change control, performance monitoring and, where outputs are not fully reliable, human review. For critical applications the draft limits use to models that are static, meaning they do not keep learning in use, and deterministic, giving the same output for the same input. That rules out generative models for critical decisions for now, while leaving room for them in non-critical support roles with human oversight.

How the two annexes relate

Annex 11 has governed computerised systems in EU GMP for years: validation, data integrity, access control, audit trails, change control and supplier assessment for any system that affects product quality. It assumes software that behaves predictably. A separate annex dedicated to AI was needed because machine learning models do not fit that assumption cleanly: their behaviour comes from data, they can be retrained, and some are not fully testable. The AI annex is designed to sit on top of Annex 11, not to replace it, so a plant applies both to an AI system.

What the AI annex adds in practice

It asks for an intended use that defines the model's scope and the data it is built for. It expects test data that is independent of training data and representative of real production, with acceptance criteria fixed before testing. It expects human oversight that is designed in, performance monitoring in operation, and change control that treats retraining as a change requiring evidence. It treats generative and adaptive models with more caution for critical uses, and it expects explainability sufficient for the people overseeing the model to understand its limits. Each of those is an addition to, not a substitute for, Annex 11's requirements.

What plants should do now

Inventory every AI model in or near the quality system and classify its criticality. For each critical model, write the intended use, the test plan and the monitoring plan in the annex's terms. Check that vendors can provide training and test data documentation, because many cannot yet. And update the computer system validation procedure so it references the AI annex where a model is involved. Plants that start now will meet inspectors who are themselves learning the annex, which is the best moment to show a considered approach.
